nodes.rationale: Wraps field commands to suppress tea.Quit: individual fields send tea.Quit on Enter for standalone use, but the wizard must intercept this to manage its own lifecycle; uses deferred evaluation so cmd() is only called inside BubbleTea's runtime.

nodes.label: Agent in clawker ps but missing from CP registry
nodes.norm_label: agent in clawker ps but missing from cp registry
nodes.rationale: Means the agent's clawkerd has not completed the Register handshake with CP — either CP was not up when the container started, or the agent's mTLS bootstrap material is invalid.

nodes.label: Container can't reach a domain
nodes.rationale: Firewall is deny-by-default; only the selected harness's egress floor is present. An allowed bare domain matches only that exact host — a blocked subdomain is a separate host; use the leading-dot wildcard form to cover subdomains. Prefer a path-scoped allow over a bare domain allow when the agent only needs specific paths.

nodes.label: Control plane down or unhealthy
nodes.rationale: CP serves its admin API only once startup checks pass (including Envoy+CoreDNS firewall bringup); a brief wait right after a cold start is expected, not a fault. CP panic traces and Ory subprocess output land in `docker logs clawker-controlplane`, not clawker's rotating logs.

nodes.label: Credentials not working (SSH/GPG/git HTTPS)
nodes.rationale: From 2026.8.3 clawker checks each enabled credential lane against the host before container start and prints one stderr warning per lane the host cannot serve. Disabled lanes are not checked; the container still starts and the failed lane fails only when used.

nodes.label: Claude Code Harness Manifest
nodes.rationale: npm-distributed, needs the node stack; managed_prompt bakes clawker's agent briefing into /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md. Staging allowlists only the portable enabledPlugins key from settings.json since the file can hold secrets/host-specific state, and plugin registry JSONs get their embedded host paths rewritten. .claude.ai denies /public/ and /share/ paths (documented UGC surfaces) so an injected prompt can't pivot the agent into fetching attacker-authored content from a trusted origin, while login/OAuth under / stays intact.

nodes.label: Codex CLI Harness Manifest
nodes.rationale: Standalone Rust binary bundling its own helpers — no stack requirement. config.toml is deliberately NOT staged because it embeds host-path-keyed state and TOML has no key-filter equivalent to json_keys; codex regenerates it on first run. chatgpt.com also serves publicly readable UGC (shared conversations), so both its http and wss rules are path-scoped to the codex backend prefix — an allow rule with no path_default puts the host in allowlist mode, denying every other path; widen only from observed blocked traffic, never preemptively.

nodes.label: OpenClaw Gateway Harness Manifest
nodes.rationale: The odd harness in the bundle: OpenClaw is a long-lived gateway daemon (CMD never exits, reached over a published port, carries a HEALTHCHECK) rather than an interactive CLI. Upstream's multi-stage source build isn't expressible as a harness fragment, so this installs the published npm tarball, whose npm-shrinkwrap.json is the one lockfile npm both publishes and honors on install (pnpm/yarn ignore it, forcing npm). Installs root-global because exec-form CMD resolves against the image PATH with no shell, so nvm/.zshenv are invisible to it. Egress floor covers only the harness's own install machinery (npm, pypi, homebrew via ghcr.io/pkg-containers path-scoped read-only to the homebrew namespace, blocking a credential-forwarding exfil channel through GHCR); model providers and channels are per-deployment choices left to the deployment repo's firewall config.

nodes.label: OpenCode Harness Manifest
nodes.rationale: Bun-compiled self-contained binary at runtime, so no stack dependency despite an npm version resolver. opencode.json and auth.json are deliberately not staged — opencode.json can embed host-path-keyed state and regenerates on first run, and credentials never travel (login happens inside the container). Minimal egress floor by design, widened only from observed blocked traffic.

nodes.label: clawker-bundle-example README
nodes.rationale: Working example bundle to fork; demonstrates every harness surface (stacks, volumes, seeds+assets, staging with json_keys/json_rewrites, path-scoped egress, npm and github-release version resolvers) via claude/codex, the minimal opencode shape, and openclaw as the odd daemon-shaped harness.

nodes.label: C/C++ Toolchain Stack
nodes.rationale: build-essential, CMake, and pkg-config via apt (distro-signature-verified). Skips itself when the image already provides g++.

nodes.label: .NET SDK Stack
nodes.rationale: Microsoft's official dotnet-install script into a system-wide DOTNET_ROOT; floats on the LTS channel unless DOTNET_CHANNEL pins a line. Skips itself when dotnet already exists.

nodes.label: Go Toolchain Stack
nodes.rationale: Official tarball, sha256-verified from the go.dev download index, installed to /usr/local/go; floats to latest stable unless GO_VERSION pins one. Uses golang-image GOPATH/PATH conventions (/go, world-writable). Skips itself when go already exists.

nodes.label: Java Toolchain Stack
nodes.rationale: Debian's default-jdk plus Maven via apt (distro-signature-verified). Skips itself when javac already exists.

nodes.label: Node.js Stack
nodes.rationale: Root-global Node LTS on /usr/local (GPG-verified prebuilt, floating patch within NODE_VERSION, trusts the OS CA bundle via NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA) with TypeScript baked root-global, plus nvm as the per-user version switcher. Baked install skips itself when an adequate node/tsc already exists; nvm skips itself when ~/.nvm exists.

nodes.label: Python Stack (uv)
nodes.rationale: uv installed system-wide on /usr/local/bin plus a uv-managed CPython resolvable as python3/python for every user. Skips the python install when python3 already exists; skips uv when already present.

nodes.label: Ruby Toolchain Stack
nodes.rationale: Debian's ruby-full plus build-essential for native gem extensions, via apt. Gems install to a shared world-writable GEM_HOME (/usr/local/share/gems). Skips itself when ruby already exists.

nodes.label: Rust Toolchain Stack (rustup)
nodes.rationale: rustup official installer, stable channel, into the user's ~/.cargo and ~/.rustup. Skips itself when cargo already exists for the user.

nodes.label: CP clock-sync error (Docker Desktop)
nodes.rationale: The Docker Desktop LinuxKit VM clock (where CP runs) can drift behind the host after sleep/wake. Rather than skew-correcting the OAuth2 assertion's iat, the CLI/bootstrap waits for the CP clock to catch up and fails fast if it doesn't converge within a timeout, avoiding the underlying Hydra 'Token used before issued' 500 caused by a future-dated assertion.

nodes.label: No release notes after upgrade
nodes.rationale: The one-time 'What's new' note shows only on the first interactive run after an upgrade and is suppressed when output is not an interactive terminal, CI is set, CLAWKER_NO_NOTIFIER is set, or the binary is a dev build. The first interactive run after adopting the feature records a baseline silently and shows nothing.

nodes.label: Rootless Docker sudo prompts
nodes.rationale: A rootless daemon requires sudo once per boot for two operations: mounting a delegated BPF filesystem so the control plane's firewall can load, and attaching an ID-mapped workspace view so a bind mount does not arrive root-owned inside the container. Views do not survive reboot, which is why the prompt repeats after each boot.

nodes.label: SSH/TCP rules route all port traffic (no domain metadata)
nodes.norm_label: ssh/tcp rules route all port traffic (no domain metadata)
nodes.rationale: Raw TCP/SSH carries no protocol-level domain metadata (unlike SNI for TLS or the Host header for HTTP), and resolving domains to IPs for per-IP routing is not viable because IPs rotate. eBPF instead creates one routing rule per port and Envoy resolves the domain at connection time, so a proto:ssh rule for one domain captures ALL port-22 traffic; with multiple SSH rules on the same port, eBPF first-match wins. Tracked as github.com/schmitthub/clawker/issues/235, deferred to the control plane.

nodes.label: Config interface
nodes.rationale: No whole-schema getter deliberately: every consumer asks for the one value it needs via storage.Get[V], keeping accessors thin and avoiding a second accessor-level default layer.

nodes.label: configImpl struct
nodes.rationale: Does not embed *storage.Store[T] because two schemas (Project, Settings) would collide on promoted verb sets; ProjectStore()/SettingsStore() are named escape hatches instead.

nodes.label: ProjectEgressRules
nodes.rationale: Deliberately excludes the harness's required egress floor, which lives in the harness bundle's harness.yaml and is composed in separately by bundler.EgressRules.

nodes.label: PrepareConfig
nodes.rationale: Only host state OUTSIDE the workspace is staged; the workspace itself arrives via mount, and credentials are never copied from the host — the token family persists in the config volume after in-container auth.

nodes.label: stageCopy (Copy Directive Semantics)
nodes.rationale: Workspace guard rejects any src match inside hostProjectRoot — the workspace is mounted, never staged, to avoid double-sourcing the same tree.

nodes.label: Builder
nodes.rationale: Two-phase build: ensures the per-project shared base image is fresh (content-hash compared) before building the harness image FROM it; base failure aborts before the harness build even starts.

nodes.label: Control Plane (CP)
nodes.rationale: Normally bootstrapped on demand the first time any command needs it (e.g. firewall status); break-glass subcommands exist for debugging, upgrades, and recovery when direct observation/manipulation is needed.

nodes.label: Per-container eBPF state
nodes.rationale: Flushed on CP shutdown (SIGTERM) so no stale map entries remain after the control plane drains its firewall stack.

nodes.label: Path-scoped egress rule
nodes.rationale: A --path is a literal prefix by default (matches also on suffixed paths) unless prefixed with ~ for an end-to-end anchored regex; --methods narrows the rule to specific HTTP methods on HTTP-family protocols only; rules accumulate and a repeated path+different action overwrites the prior action.

nodes.label: Firewall bypass (server-side timed override)
nodes.rationale: Grants a container unrestricted egress for a duration; expiry is tracked server-side so it survives CLI exit, and enforcement auto re-enables when the timer lapses.

nodes.label: CoreDNS (DNS-level allow/deny)
nodes.rationale: Enforces domain-level egress rules at the DNS layer, paired with Envoy for SNI-layer enforcement.

nodes.label: Envoy (TLS SNI filtering proxy)
nodes.rationale: Enforces domain-level egress rules via TLS SNI filtering as part of the shared firewall stack on the clawker Docker network.

nodes.label: Firewall rule store
nodes.rationale: Shared across projects; prune wipes and re-syncs from the current project config only (other projects' rules are removed too and must be restored via refresh or next container start); a failed prune restores the previous rules so it never leaves the store empty.

nodes.label: Firewall CA certificate / TLS inspection
nodes.rationale: CA keypair and all domain certs used for TLS inspection; rotating it requires rebuilding and recreating running containers to pick up the new CA.

nodes.rationale: cmdutil/output.go helpers (HandleError, PrintError, PrintWarning, PrintNextSteps, PrintStatus, OutputJSON, PrintHelpHint) are all deprecated in favor of direct fmt.Fprintf with ColorScheme.

nodes.label: cli-output Skill

nodes.label: clawkerd Package Guide (AGENTS.md)
nodes.rationale: clawkerd is per-container PID 1 init AND the CP-dialed mTLS command listener on :7700; it forks the container's user CMD as PID 1's only direct child on CP-dispatched AgentReady, with privilege drop done kernel-side (setgroups→setgid→setuid) in the spawned child between fork and exec, not by clawkerd dropping its own root — it stays root for log rotation, bootstrap reads, orphan reaping, and future privileged operations.

nodes.label: controlplane/AGENTS.md — Control-plane safety section
nodes.rationale: Defines the failure rules shared by CP and every CP-adjacent binary: no panic/log.Fatal/os.Exit on the boot or serve path, every long-lived goroutine recovers, and subsystems degrade with event=<subsystem>_unavailable rather than crash the process.

nodes.label: Root CLAUDE.md — 'CP crashing is a SECURITY incident, not an availability one'
nodes.norm_label: root claude.md — 'cp crashing is a security incident, not an availability one'
nodes.rationale: A CP crash leaves pinned eBPF firewall state without supervision, so a CP (or clawkerd, PID 1 of the agent container) crash is framed as a security incident rather than a mere availability blip — motivating the strict no-panic/no-Fatal/no-os.Exit resilience contract on boot and serve paths.

nodes.label: clawkerd Resilience Contract
nodes.rationale: clawkerd is PID 1 of the agent container, so an escaping panic kills the whole container. Hard rules: no panic()/log.Fatal()/os.Exit() outside two named exceptions; every long-lived goroutine wraps defer recoverGoroutine; subsystem failures degrade rather than cascade (a broken spawn entry returns Error{IO_ERROR} and the supervisor stays alive); every degraded path emits a structured event=<name> log line so triage works from logs alone.

nodes.label: netlogger OTLP circuit breaker
nodes.rationale: netlogger is engineered to fail open with respect to firewall enforcement: three consecutive Export() failures permanently trip the breaker for the CP's lifetime with no background reconnect, because telemetry availability is deliberately binary per-CP-lifetime rather than silently degraded; enforcement itself is unaffected either way.

nodes.label: Three-tier component resolution model

Qualified names resolve only from the declared/installed bundle set. All three tiers are enumerated identically by convention directory (harnesses/<name>/, stacks/<name>/, monitoring/<name>/) with no bare-manifest-at-root special case.

nodes.label: Docker socket shared-responsibility risk
nodes.rationale: Docker-outside-of-Docker (the real host socket) was chosen over Docker-in-Docker for performance and reliability, despite being a major privilege-escalation vector (root-equivalent host control), because DinD needs a nested daemon, consumes far more resources, and has storage-driver issues. Users are told to treat any session with socket access as supervised.

nodes.label: Git hooks host-code-execution vector
nodes.rationale: A git hook the agent plants in a bind-mounted repo's .git/hooks runs harmlessly inside the container, but the same .git directory is bind-mounted from the host, so the next host-side git command executes the planted hook on the host with the user's privileges. Snapshot mode avoids this because its .git copy is disposable and never reaches the host; bind mode and worktree containers currently leave this gap open.

nodes.label: Prompt injection (deny-the-connection philosophy)
nodes.rationale: Clawker deliberately does not try to detect or filter prompt injection, and does not inspect egress traffic content, because content-based exfiltration detection (across all protocols/ports/sizes, against obfuscated/encrypted payloads) is an unwinnable arms race. Instead it denies the connection entirely: the injection can change the agent's intent but not the container's network constraints.

nodes.label: GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false in worktrees
nodes.rationale: Go's VCS stamping only recognizes a .git directory, but a linked worktree has a .git file, so the go tool walks up to the mounted main .git where stamping would either fail (exit status 128) or record the wrong revision. Worktree containers set GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false to avoid this; override via agent.env when needed.

nodes.label: Worktree host-path mirroring for session persistence
nodes.norm_label: worktree host-path mirroring for session persistence
nodes.rationale: When --worktree is used, the worktree is mounted at its host absolute path rather than a generic /workspace, because Claude Code discovers sessions by matching the container's working directory against git worktree paths; a synthetic path would break session resume.

nodes.rationale: to_json refuses to write graph.json when the new graph is smaller than the existing one, preventing accidental data loss.

nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge; use AMBIGUOUS when unsure; always show token cost; never hide cohesion scores; warn before HTML viz on >5000 nodes.

nodes.label: CLI-CP trust chain
nodes.rationale: The CLI is the trust orchestrator: it generates all cryptographic material (CA, signing key, client cert, server cert) and bind-mounts only the public halves into the CP container. The CLI private signing key is NEVER mounted into the container, so Hydra verifies private_key_jwt assertions against the registered public JWK only, keeping the signing capability host-only.

nodes.label: coredns-clawker otel plugin
nodes.rationale: OTEL log exporter for DNS query events — emits structured dns.query log records over OTLP/gRPC + mTLS to the CP-only collector.

nodes.label: Linked stdlib CoreDNS plugins (forward/health/log/reload/template)
nodes.rationale: coremain does not transitively import stdlib plugins — CoreDNS's zplugin.go blank-imports must be replicated per binary. Only the plugins the firewall Corefile actually uses are imported, avoiding the full stdlib import set (Azure, AWS, K8s, etc.).

nodes.label: coredns-clawker Binary Guide
nodes.rationale: Custom CoreDNS build embedding two in-tree plugins, built as a static Linux binary and go:embed'd into the clawker release; firewall.Stack builds the clawker-coredns image from that asset on demand. Not invoked from the host CLI — runs only inside the CP-managed CoreDNS container. Plugin chain order is deliberate: otel first so it observes the final response after every other plugin has produced its rcode/answer set; dnsbpf second so it still wraps all resolver plugins (forward, hosts) and intercepts A answers before they leave the process for the BPF dns_cache map.

nodes.label: Privilege Model (clawkerd root, user CMD unprivileged)
nodes.norm_label: privilege model (clawkerd root, user cmd unprivileged)

nodes.label: Agent Awareness Prompt
nodes.rationale: Baking a managed-context prompt into the image gives the agent self-service awareness of firewall/network boundaries so it can diagnose blocked domains and suggest the right clawker firewall command instead of the user manually troubleshooting.

nodes.label: clawkerd: The Container's PID 1
nodes.rationale: clawkerd stays root to own signal handling, zombie reaping (Wait4(-1)), the mTLS listener, and log writes; the user CMD is forked with SysProcAttr.Credential so the kernel drops privilege atomically between fork and exec.

nodes.label: Credential Forwarding (HTTPS/SSH/GPG/gitconfig)
nodes.rationale: Host credentials (HTTPS via host proxy, SSH/GPG via socket bridge) are brokered rather than copied into the container, keeping keys on the host.

nodes.label: Firewall Decoupling
nodes.rationale: eBPF cgroup programs are attached from outside by the control plane, not configured inside the container, so the image stays portable and a compromised user CMD (no NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW, cap_add: []) cannot modify or bypass firewall enforcement.

nodes.label: Two-Stage Build (base image + harness image)
nodes.rationale: Splitting into a harness-agnostic base and a per-harness image lets rebuilding one harness reuse the existing base whenever its content hash is unchanged, avoiding redundant apt/tooling layers across harnesses.

nodes.label: Firewall (deny-by-default egress)
nodes.rationale: eBPF cgroup programs attached from outside redirect outbound TCP to Envoy while CoreDNS returns NXDOMAIN for unlisted domains, combining the harness's minimal egress floor with per-project rules.

nodes.label: The Padded Cell
nodes.rationale: Clawker protects everything outside the container from what happens inside (host filesystem, host network, other Docker resources) while not inheriting Docker's full threat model — if Docker allows a command, Clawker permits it, but only against Clawker-managed resources.

nodes.label: Resource Identification (labels authoritative)
nodes.rationale: Clawker refuses to operate on resources without dev.clawker.managed=true even if they carry the clawker. name prefix, making labels the authoritative source of truth over naming.

nodes.label: Config Write Provenance Tracking
nodes.rationale: Writes route back to the file a field originally came from, with atomic temp-file+fsync+rename and advisory locking, so edits via the interactive editor don't clobber unrelated layers or race concurrent clawker processes.

nodes.label: Agent Registry (sqlite)
nodes.rationale: Keyed by SHA-256 of the mTLS leaf cert thumbprint plus container ID; CP is the sole writer so agent identity is auditable and cannot be self-attested.

nodes.label: Agent Watcher + Clean Self-Shutdown
nodes.rationale: Drain-to-zero (60s grace + 2 consecutive zero-count polls) triggers an ordered drain callback so eBPF state is flushed and OTLP batches complete before BPF maps go away; on-failure restart policy does not retrigger clean shutdown.

nodes.label: Control Plane Container Privileges
nodes.rationale: CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_BPF, RW /sys/fs/bpf, RO /sys/fs/cgroup, and Docker socket access are needed to attach cgroup eBPF programs and drive sibling firewall containers; these privileges are never extended to agent containers, which run with cap_add: [] and full seccomp/AppArmor confinement.

nodes.label: Control Plane (clawkercp)
nodes.rationale: CP is not the firewall; disabling firewall.enable does not disable CP, mTLS, or the agent registry. CP is the always-on authoritative supervisor for every clawker-managed agent on the host.

nodes.label: CP Guarantees
nodes.rationale: Deterministic eBPF ownership, auditable agent identity via server-captured cert thumbprints, real containment via long-lived Session dispatch, and centralized short-lived OAuth2 auth.

nodes.label: Path Mirroring
nodes.rationale: Coding-agent harnesses (e.g. Claude Code) key session state off the working directory; mirroring the host's real path inside the container makes /resume's git-worktree-based session discovery work, whereas a synthetic /workspace path would break it.

nodes.label: How /resume Works (claude harness)
nodes.rationale: Path mirroring makes the container cwd match the identifier Claude Code uses to store and discover sessions; a synthetic path would break /resume entirely.

nodes.label: Worktree Support
nodes.rationale: A worktree's .git file references the main repo's .git/worktrees/<name> metadata by absolute host path, so clawker bind-mounts the main repo's .git directory at its identical original path so the reference resolves inside the container.

nodes.label: DockerHost accessor
nodes.rationale: $DOCKER_HOST wins over the docker.host setting because that env var is the docker CLI's own contract; falls back to the active docker context, the only place a rootless install records its daemon address.

nodes.label: docker/context package
nodes.rationale: Read-only reader of the docker CLI's own context files, because a rootless install records its daemon address there and nowhere else — DOCKER_HOST says nothing about it.

nodes.label: NewClient
nodes.rationale: WithEnvHost() skips DockerHost resolution and leaves the address to the SDK's own env lookup — the CP daemon's own option, since host-side settings/context must never be consulted in-container.

nodes.label: PTYHandler
nodes.rationale: Restore() unconditionally undoes visual modes an in-container TUI enables but can't undo on abrupt end (Ctrl-P+Q detach / kill); alt-screen leave is the lone gated exception because its DECRC cursor-restore squashes primary-screen output when emitted blind.

nodes.label: Git safe.directory=* wildcard config
nodes.rationale: Wildcard trust prevents dubious-ownership errors from VirtioFS reporting a different mount owner and covers submodules/nested repos an exact-path entry would miss; safe because the container has no other unprivileged user for the check to protect against.

nodes.label: ProjectMigrations / SettingsMigrations
nodes.rationale: Migrations run per file layer at load time; a failed rewrite degrades to in-memory migration with a warning rather than losing the migration silently.

nodes.label: validateProjectNodes
nodes.rationale: Front-door validation walks each discovered layer (never the merged tree) so errors name the actual file; a bad harness/stack/bundle name fails the whole constructor, not a partial/degraded Config.

nodes.label: EnsureHarnessVolume
nodes.rationale: An existing MANAGED volume whose harness label names a different harness is refused (ownership failsafe); an unlabeled managed occupant is silently adopted because the label is forgeable and Docker cannot retro-label a local volume.

nodes.label: HarnessVolumeName
nodes.rationale: Validates the harness segment (bare or qualified) and volume segment separately then joins via consts.JoinIdentity, keeping the composition injective for a fixed (project, agent) pair since every token is dot-free.

nodes.label: GenConfigDoc
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for config field metadata across projects and settings — reflection-driven from the same yaml/label/desc/default/required struct tags used by JSON Schema generation.

nodes.label: GenJSONSchema
nodes.rationale: Recurses into struct-slice element types (unlike storage.NormalizeFields) so array items carry full property schemas; objects are additionalProperties:false so editors flag unknown keys.

nodes.label: GenMarkdownTree / GenMarkdownTreeWebsite
nodes.rationale: GenMarkdownTreeWebsite exists separately from GenMarkdownTreeCustom to produce MDX-safe output — EscapeMDXProse guards bare <word> angle brackets from being parsed as JSX tags.

nodes.label: CheckURLAgainstEgressRules (egress_check.go)
nodes.rationale: Closes a proven exfil vector: a container agent could otherwise encode stolen secrets in URL query params and use the host browser as an out-of-band channel, bypassing the Envoy+CoreDNS firewall entirely.

nodes.label: consts.ValidateHarnessRef
nodes.rationale: Shared closed-vocabulary validator for harness/overlay name spelling (bare or namespace.bundle.component), used both by config's write front-door and by docker's volume-naming package to keep names addressable and injective.

nodes.label: egress-rules.yaml test fixture
nodes.rationale: Regex allowlist/denylist path rules are commented to explain they must enforce identically to Envoy's safe_regex, including RFC 3986 remove_dot_segments canonicalization, so the host proxy denies the same paths Envoy would (and never allows what Envoy denies).

nodes.label: Schema-URL header stamping
nodes.rationale: Derivation lives in config, not the Factory, because NewConfig is called directly by every binary (CLI, CP, host proxy, bridge) and all must stamp the same header for the same build; the ref is always frozen, never a branch.

nodes.label: Container/volume naming convention
nodes.rationale: Harness-scoped volume names include the harness's exact selection spelling so two harnesses that declare the same volume name (both shipped harnesses declare 'config') never land on one volume.

nodes.label: Two-tier fail-closed design
nodes.rationale: A policy deny (URL not allow-listed) is a 403 warn; a broken rules file is an infrastructure fault (500, log.Error) — never a silent skip. Action validation uses !EqualFold(action,'allow') so typos fail closed.

nodes.label: compilePathRegex regex lockstep with Envoy
nodes.rationale: Compiles a ~-path to the same full-string-anchored RE2 form Envoy's safe_regex uses; a pattern that fails to compile rejects the whole rules file, mirroring Envoy refusing a bad safe_regex config.

nodes.label: Route Identity Contract
nodes.rationale: Keying dns_cache writes by the zone's CP-allocated identity (not the query name) is what makes wildcard zones work: all subdomains map to the one identity route_map is keyed on; sticky identities keep dns_cache and route_map keyspaces from drifting.

nodes.label: Shared BPF Map Lifecycle (sync.Once singleton)
nodes.rationale: No OnShutdown close handler: CoreDNS's reload plugin tears down and rebuilds server blocks without restarting the process, so closing the FD on shutdown would invalidate it permanently since sync.Once won't re-execute; the FD is deliberately leaked for the process lifetime.

nodes.label: BPFMap.Update write precedence
nodes.rationale: Cilium ipcache source-precedence analog: DNS-derived writes never overwrite a DNSSourceSeed entry owned by CP SyncRoutes; a Lookup failure other than ErrKeyNotExist skips the write since the source is unknown and writing could clobber a seed.

nodes.rationale: Discrete rubric values (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) chosen because models follow discrete rubrics better than continuous ranges; production data showed collapse to 0.5 and 0.85+ bimodal distribution under a continuous range.

nodes.rationale: Full repo-relative path with every directory level kept must match the AST extractor's ID scheme, or re-extraction creates orphan ghost-duplicate nodes; old immediate-parent-format projects need graphify extract --force.

nodes.label: source_file Verbatim Rule
nodes.rationale: Copying the FILE_LIST path verbatim keeps the full build and incremental --update on the same base, so build_merge's replace-on-re-extract matches the existing node instead of accumulating a duplicate.

nodes.label: build_merge() Function
nodes.rationale: Reads graph.json directly without a NetworkX round-trip so edge direction (calls/implements/imports) is always preserved (#801).

nodes.label: Constrained Query Expansion (Step 0)
nodes.rationale: graphify query matches via case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming or synonyms; expanding the question against the graph's own vocabulary first avoids collapsing to zero hits on wording mismatch, without inventing tokens.

nodes.label: Project Name Normalization
nodes.rationale: Directory-derived slugs may be invalid Docker identifiers or undesirable; the name field lets a project opt out of automatic slugging for container/volume names and cert SAN identity.

nodes.label: Project Registration
nodes.rationale: Registration in registry.yaml is how walk-up discovery knows where to stop climbing the directory tree.

nodes.label: Layered Configuration System
nodes.rationale: Layered discovery (walk-up + explicit user dir + defaults) with closest-to-CWD-wins merge rules lets a subdirectory override only the fields it names, enabling monorepo and per-directory overrides without duplicating shared config.

nodes.label: CP Troubleshooting
nodes.rationale: Clock-sync failures happen because the CLI mints the bootstrap assertion against the host clock while Hydra validates iat against CP's (possibly VM-drifted) clock with zero leeway; rather than re-mint or skew-correct, the CLI waits for CP's clock to converge before letting the container start.

nodes.label: Per-Harness Build Overlays
nodes.rationale: build.harnesses.<name> lets you scope extra stacks, packages, or inject steps to one harness's image without touching the harness definition or the base, e.g. registering an MCP server only in the claude image instead of every harness image.

nodes.label: Stacks (reusable language-runtime definitions)
nodes.rationale: Stacks are self-guarding — each skips itself when the image already provides the runtime — so a project-declared stack and a harness-declared stack sharing a name render safely without double-installation.

nodes.label: SetupWorktree
nodes.rationale: go-git's experimental worktree package does not enforce the native git worktree add interlock against double-checkout of one branch, so SetupWorktree adds ErrBranchAlreadyCheckedOut itself — without it, two checkouts could share one branch ref and a commit in either would slide the other's HEAD.

nodes.label: WorktreeDirProvider interface
nodes.rationale: Dependency inversion for filesystem layout: internal/git stays a Tier 1 leaf with no config-package dependency, so the caller (internal/project) supplies directory resolution.

nodes.label: Branch/remote dwim resolution
nodes.rationale: Mirrors native git worktree add with no network: local head wins, else explicit base, else the dwim rule for exactly-one-matching remote, else new local branch from HEAD; detached HEAD is intentionally unsupported since branch is the worktree identity by design.

nodes.rationale: When --agent is provided, container/exec/cp target names resolve to clawker.<project>.<agent>, with project resolved from the current directory; --name overrides this for create.

nodes.label: Harness (agent runtime)
nodes.rationale: The agent runtime an image is built for, picked at build time with 'clawker build -t <harness>' and at run time with the '@:<harness>' selector; bare names resolve from the embedded floor and loose convention directories, qualified namespace.bundle.harness names resolve from installed bundles.

nodes.label: Container Lifecycle (four host-side phases + CP-driven init)
nodes.norm_label: container lifecycle (four host-side phases + cp-driven init)
nodes.rationale: Creating a container never contacts CP (bootstrap material is minted against the host clock); the CP readiness and clock-sync gate is enforced only later, on the start path, before clawkerd exchanges the baked-in assertion.

nodes.label: clawker volume prune
nodes.rationale: clawker volume prune removes ALL unused agent volumes (workspace, config, history) by default, which can lose config/history if the matching agent container is not running at prune time; --all widens further to infra volumes. Targeted cleanup via volume list + volume remove is the safer alternative.

nodes.label: ensureEgressRulesReady
nodes.rationale: Three-stage sequential gate (firewall container running -> Envoy healthy -> rules file valid); each stage only starts once the prior passes so a later stage never races ahead of its prerequisite.

nodes.label: CP-before-hostproxy startup ordering
nodes.rationale: Control plane and firewall stack boot before the host proxy so its readiness gate can assume the firewall is already coming up instead of racing it — starting host proxy first would deadlock cold start since its gate waits on the firewall.

nodes.label: Credential Injection Proxy
nodes.rationale: Host secrets are never copied into the sandbox; the agent receives phantom tokens and a local reverse proxy injects real keys on the fly, so a compromised agent cannot extract credentials.

nodes.label: Egress Domain Allowlist
nodes.rationale: Network access is open by default; restriction is opt-in via network.block/--allow-domain, so exfiltration is contained only once a profile enables it.

nodes.label: Nono
nodes.rationale: OS-level least-privilege sandbox for coding-agent CLIs; supervisor + credential proxy; irreversible Landlock/Seatbelt floor with fail-closed network policy.

nodes.label: Key Hostproxy Findings
nodes.rationale: Zero auth on all endpoints, newline injection in git credential protocol format, arbitrary port binding via /callback/register, git credential extraction for any host.

nodes.label: Debounce Mechanism (default 3s)
nodes.rationale: Waits until file activity stops before triggering, so a wave of parallel agent writes doesn't trigger a rebuild per file.

nodes.label: Control-plane safety failure rules
nodes.rationale: No panic, log.Fatal, or os.Exit on the boot or serve path; every long-lived goroutine recovers; subsystems degrade with event=<subsystem>_unavailable — because a CP crash leaves pinned eBPF state without supervision.

nodes.label: Key Design Decisions
nodes.rationale: whail as the sole Docker SDK isolation layer, labels as authoritative ownership, stdout/stderr stream separation for scriptability, Factory DI, Docker as source of truth for runtime state vs local YAML for config, config.Config as a lazy gateway, and zerolog restricted to file-only logging.

nodes.norm_label: two-layer color palette (named colors + semantic theme)
nodes.rationale: Layer 1 named colors are canonical hex values that never change; Layer 2 semantic aliases (ColorPrimary, ColorError, etc.) reference Layer 1, so intent-based usage in command code stays stable if the underlying hex ever moves.

nodes.label: Why an ID-mapped mount
nodes.rationale: Docker has no per-mount ID mapping (moby#52061 proposed one and was closed unimplemented) and podman's --userns=keep-id has no Docker equivalent since podman is daemonless; chowning the tree works but is mutually exclusive with live two-way bind-mode editing. The kernel's mount_setattr(2) ID-mapped mount gives both sides native ownership simultaneously with no files modified.

nodes.label: Rootless Docker uid mapping formula
nodes.rationale: Container uid 0 maps to the daemon user's own host uid; container uid n>=1 maps to subuid_base + n - 1, walking /etc/subuid ranges in file order. Refusals (root-owned workspace, no subordinate ranges, id beyond ranges) are explicit because a wrong mapping is worse than none.

nodes.label: term -> iostreams -> factory terminal-behavior cascade
nodes.rationale: Three layers separate concerns: term reports capabilities (TERM/COLORTERM/NO_COLOR), iostreams builds standard terminal UX behavior on top, and factory applies clawker-specific preference overrides (CLAWKER_SPINNER_DISABLED).

nodes.rationale: Two kernel-cooperation gaps (BPF filesystem delegation for the firewall, ID-mapped workspace views) are bridged with a one-time-per-boot sudo-run embedded helper so nothing is permanently installed on the host.

nodes.label: ResolveImageWithSource
nodes.rationale: Scopes deliberately do not ladder — a project with no built image never falls back to the global image, and there is no fallback to the bare build.Image base, which is never runnable as an agent.

nodes.rationale: A panic on a CP-reachable code path crashes CP PID 1, skips Stack.Stop + ebpfMgr.FlushAll, and leaves eBPF programs pinned with no supervisor -- silent firewall failure.
